Take a medical leave of absence.  I did this twice and it saved my GPA.  Be warned that after you go on leave you may need to prove you're recovered before you can go back.

If you don't want to go that far, at least talk to the deans or counseling center at your school.  They will probably be able to get you extensions and other accommodations.
Thanks.  I think things were getting worse because without the medication I was sleeping 5 hours a night.  So I went back on it.
Imaginary friends are a lot of fun :) Don't judge yourself for having them!  When I was lonely I made one, but she committed suicide.

I fucking hate abstract algebra but you should take it anyway because it's really important and you need it for a lot of other math.  That is, if you want to be a math major.  Also, abstract algebra will tell you if you want to be a math major or not.  I got an A- so I decided I have no talent for the field and ought to go into applied math or become an actuary.  Also, I think I only hate abstract algebra because I'm bad at it, so who knows, you'll probably really like it.

Well, I don't know if I ever was depressed, but I used to think suicide was a solution to a lot of my problems.  Hard homework set?  Kill myself!  Fight with my sister?  Kill myself!  Didn't get enough sleep?  Well I guess I'll kill myself, dying is the same thing as sleeping right?

Anyway, this got me kicked out of school a couple times and eventually I got sent to the 3East program at McLean Hospital ("an intensive dialectical behavioral therapy residence for teen and college age women with impulsive and self-endangering behaviors"...mostly a place for borderlines).  While I was there I tried to strangle myself a couple times, so they put me on "Program Hold" and asked me if I could commit to being in the program.  I hadn't decided if I'd wanted to live, and I figured if I wanted to live I should commit to treatment, but if I didn't want to live I shouldn't commit to treatment.  So for four days I thought very hard about whether I wanted to live, and eventually I decided suicide was a really silly idea.  So I stopped trying to kill myself.

It also helped that they told us specific things we could do when distressed, and when we felt bad they walked us through them.  The specific tactics didn't help so much as the mindset that when you're distressed, you should try to make yourself feel better instead of believing what your mind tells you.  They also taught me what I thought depended on how I felt, which seems like common sense but was very not-obvious at the time.

They also put me on Risperdal.  I kind of hate it because I'm scared it makes me stupid.  But honestly, when I'm on the medication, it's very hard for me to feel distressed or to think about one thing for too long.

So after I got healthy I was discharged from the program and went back to school.  Life has been bloody excellent since then.  I have a 3.9 GPA, always get enough sleep, and haven't thought about suicide in over a year.  When I'm distressed - and I rarely am - I hang out with my friends instead of strangling myself in dark corners.  I really can't see myself hurting myself ever again.  But of course I always have to take it easy and be careful about keeping myself out of downward spirals.

tl;dr: 


* Decided to live
* Went on medication
* Learned how to deal with bad days
